variants.headline: Party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}.
variants.body:
The leader of {party}, {leader}, has blundered in an election debate. The misstep is established, but the words involved and their effect on voters are not supplied here. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the debate event from a fabricated quotation or a claim that the election's outcome has been decided.

A leader has blundered in a debate. Tempting material for a perfect quotation, except the words are not supplied here. The mistake is news enough. Readers can judge a performance without being given an invented audience, a fictional blush or a claim that the whole election is suddenly over.

The performance of {target} deserves examination without assuming an electoral effect. This paper records the blunder and leaves the words involved and the public's response outside its factual account where they are unspecified. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
